rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance: annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement:
Annual residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% or 80% of the percent change in the CPI over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI change is negative, no increase is allowed.

Published rate:
- The City publishes the allowable increase by June 30 each year, effective September 1.
- The maximum allowable increase is 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

Petitions:
- An owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the cap. The owner must show that a larger increase is needed for a fair and reasonable return.
- The City Manager or designee decides within 60 days of a complete application.
- Tenants may petition about increases above the maximum, reduced housing services, habitability failures, unauthorized or excessive capital-improvement pass-throughs, and other violations.

Notice and fees:
- Owners must give written notice of the Ordinance and tenant rights at the start of a lease or with any rent-increase notice.
- Landlords may, but need not, charge a registration-fee pass-through. It is charged per rental unit, not per tenant. A landlord who charges more than $50 must reimburse the overpayment.
rules.key_value: Lower of 3% or 80% of 12-month CPI change; no increase if CPI is negative; 2.87% for Sept 1, 2026 through Aug 31, 2027; registration-fee pass-through capped at $50 per unit

coverage.summary: Residential rental buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before January 1, 1990. Buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 and mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990 are exempt. On covered units this cap is stricter than the state cap, so the state cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12(d)(3)) yields to it. Exempt units may still fall under the state cap if that law's own conditions are met.
coverage.construction_date_basis: Date the building was 'constructed'; the source does not say which record (year built, certificate of occupancy) controls.
coverage.other_conditions: Mobile home spaces are covered only if offered for rent on or before January 1, 1990.

rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.effective_date_note: The City Council adopted the ordinance on an undated Tuesday night, and it took effect November 19, 2021. Each year's allowable increase is published by June 30 and takes effect September 1. The 2.87% rate runs from September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.

rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
rules.review_note: No Santa Ana Municipal Code section appears in the documents, so the citation is by ordinance name. The cutoff basis is recorded as year_built because the source says only 'constructed'. D084 does not clearly say whether the $50 pass-through cap is monthly or annual; its calculator multiplies a monthly fee by 12.
rules.source_notes: D085 is the official City news release on adoption; it gives the formula, cutoff, petition and notice rules. D084 is the official Rent Stabilization page; it gives the current 2.87% rate, the petition types and the pass-through rule. DX19 mentions the ordinance only in passing. D084:c1 listed 2027-08-31 as a sunset date, but that is only the end of the annual rate period, so it is removed. The cell candidate's certificate_of_occupancy basis is not stated in any source.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
If a landlord charges a tenant a pass-through fee greater than $50, the landlord shall reimburse the tenant for the registration fee pass-through overpayment.
The City was the first in Orange County to approve a rent stabilization ordinance limiting rent increases for certain types of residential properties and creating new protections against eviction.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement:
After a tenancy has lasted 30 days, an owner may not terminate it without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice.

Causes:
- At-fault causes include default in rent, breach of a material lease term, nuisance, criminal activity and other actions.
- No-fault causes include the owner's intent to occupy, removal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.

Notice and relocation:
- Before serving an at-fault termination notice, the owner must first give notice of the violation and a period to fix it.
- For a no-fault termination, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
- Owners had to notify existing tenants of these protections before December 19, 2021. They must also notify tenants at the start or renewal of a lease.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days of tenancy; notice and time to cure before an at-fault termination; no-fault termination requires 3 months' relocation assistance or waiver of the final 3 months' rent

coverage.summary: Residential rental property in Santa Ana. The listed exemptions include housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters. Where it qualifies under Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(i), it applies instead of the state just-cause law.

coverage.other_conditions: Applies after 30 days of tenancy. The exemption list is introduced with 'including', so it may not be exhaustive.

rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance was adopted on an undated Tuesday night and took effect November 19, 2021. The deadline for notifying existing tenants was December 19, 2021.

rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
rules.review_note: No Municipal Code section is given. The ordinance was adopted after Sept. 1, 2019. Under Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(i) it displaces state just-cause only if it is more protective and contains a binding finding saying so. Its terms (30 days instead of 12 months; 3 months' relocation instead of 1) look more protective, but the finding cannot be checked without the ordinance text. The 15-year exemption gives no reference date, so whether it rolls is unknown.
rules.source_notes: D085 is the official City news release on adoption. D084 is the official City page summary. DX19 mentions eviction protections only in passing and attributes them to the rent stabilization ordinance; the official release shows they are in the separate Just Cause Eviction Ordinance. The cell candidate's note that the exemption list was truncated is wrong: D085 gives the full list.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
If your landlord evicts you for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for your moving costs.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Ord. NS-3090)
rules.requirement:
The ordinance prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting software ('Algorithmic Devices') for residential rental property in Santa Ana. It targets tools that set rents using nonpublic competitor data such as real-time rents, lease renewals and occupancy levels.

Exclusions: software that relies solely on publicly available data or aggregate historical data, and tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.

Enforcement:
- An affected tenant may sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
- The tenant need only prove that the landlord used prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
- Per a law-firm alert, violations accrue per month.
- The City will mostly use its existing code enforcement system.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data; tenant civil action; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (per month per DX06) plus attorney's fees

coverage.summary: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits. No size, age or owner exemptions are stated. The ordinance is designed to operate alongside state antitrust law (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729), not to displace it.
coverage.other_conditions: Does not cover software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data, or affordable-housing compliance tools.

rules.exemptions: Pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data or aggregate historical data; tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.effective_date_note: First reading was approved Feb. 17, 2026 and the final vote was set for March 3, 2026 (DX19). DX18 reports that the final Tuesday vote completed adoption. A law-firm alert (DX06) gives the effective date as April 2, 2026, which is 30 days after March 3. All sources are secondary.
citation_aliases: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.review_note: Every source is secondary. The ordinance text, Municipal Code section and definition of 'Algorithmic Device' are not captured. The March 3, 2026 adoption date is inferred from the scheduled final vote and DX18's report that the final Tuesday vote completed adoption.
rules.source_notes: DX19 (a City press release republished by PublicCEO; same URL as link-only D087) predates the final vote, which is why DX19:c1 was marked pending. DX18 (OCBJ; same URL as link-only D086) and DX06 confirm adoption and the effective date, so this is the same ordinance and is now in force. The Apartment Association of Orange County criticism in DX18 is opinion and does not raise a preemption question.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
does not apply to pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
Under the ordinance, a tenant affected by a violation may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney’s fees.
Landlords caught using the banned software could be fined $1,000. The measure passed its first vote on Feb. 17, and Tuesday’s vote was the final step to officially put the ordinance into effect.
